titleStmt.title: Kephalaia of the Teacher, edition page 45: diplomatic and Leiden transcription

sourceDesc.bibl: Kephalaia (Manichäische Handschriften der Staatlichen Museen Berlin), ed. H. J. Polotsky and A. Böhlig, Stuttgart: Kohlhammer, 45. Restorations, sublinear dots, gap counts and corrections are the editors'.

encodingDesc.p: EpiDoc. Read by eye from the page image; gap counts, sublinear dots and supralinear stroke extents verified by measurement on the image. A supralinear stroke is marked on every letter it covers by at least half its width. Spaces are the edition's word division. Facsimile zones are measured line centres. The editors' German statements are not transcribed: each is mapped to an id of the controlled vocabulary data/kephalaia/editorial_vocabulary.json and carried as @ana (ed: statements in the text, app: apparatus footnotes, tr: categories of the transcriber's commentary).

div.p: The framed manuscript page number [ⲙⲉ] (top right) is printed in restoration brackets with a bar above and below as the frame, not as a supralinear stroke; the running title ⲙⲡⲥⲁϩ has a dot under ⲙ. Twelve illegible dots at the line end (880–1171). No strokes.
Dot under ⲙ of ⲙⲡⲱⲛϩ (575); three illegible dots at the line end (1202–1255). No strokes.
The whole line is 29 illegible dots (568–1310).
The whole line is 29 illegible dots (569–1312; 1127–1206 small, area 4–6).

"leer" after ⲛⲓⲱⲧ → vac.; "geringe Spuren" after ⲡⲛⲟⲙⲟⲥ → the editors' statement for the rest of the line (traces, illegible). The strokes tool reports a bar inside the German (1069–1078); no Coptic strokes.

Two illegible dots (712, 738), one inside the brackets (774), one after them (809). Stroke over the free-standing first ⲛ of ⲛⲛⲉⲧⲁⲛⲓⲧ (931–944). Measured stroke over ⲙⲛ (1087–1107, pixel row): ⲙ 52 %, ⲛ 60 %, encoded on both.

Dots under ⲧ of ⲧⲁⲥ (574), ⲁ and ⲥ of ⲁⲥϯ (788, 805), ⲡ and ⲟ of ⲙⲡⲟⲩⲁⲓ[ⲛⲉ] (1081, 1098); three illegible dots (705–757). Stroke over the first ⲛ of ⲛⲛⲁⲓⲱⲛ (935–948). Measured stroke over the restored ⲙⲛ (1257–1277, pixel row): ⲙ 52 %, ⲛ 60 %, encoded on both.
Stroke over ⲃ of ⲁⲥⲑⲃⲓⲟ (731–744). Measured stroke over ⲛⲛ of ⲛⲛⲃⲉⲝⲉⲩⲉ (794–812, pixel row): ⲛ 53 %, ⲛ 57 %, encoded on both. Fourteen illegible dots at the line end (930–1273).
The line ends in a closing bracket after ⲧⲟⲩ with no opening bracket on this line or at the end of l. 8; ⲧⲟⲩ is encoded as read and the bracket as an unpaired sign (ledger §4, 29.28).
27 illegible dots (569–1257) before ⲧⲟⲩ. No strokes.
The line ends in a closing bracket after ⲙ with no opening bracket on the line; ⲙ is encoded as read and the bracket as an unpaired sign (as l. 9).

"leer" after ⲛϩⲁⲉ → vac., followed by three illegible dots (1222–1275).

Dots under ⲙ of ⲙⲁⲩ (574), ⲡ before the bracket (703) and ⲉ after it (768). Measured stroke over ϩⲛ (651–670, pixel row): ϩ 50 %, ⲛ 60 %, encoded on both. Reconcile also counts specks of the German "leer" (1150–1181, area ≤ 7) — they lie above the zone floor and are not dots.
One illegible dot at the line start (569), six after ⲛϭⲁⲙ (691–824). Stroke over ⲛ of ⲛϭⲁⲙ (596–608).
A closing bracket follows ⲧⲏ with no opening bracket on the line or at the end of l. 12; ⲧⲏ is encoded as read and the bracket as an unpaired sign (as ll. 9–10).
Nine illegible dots at the line start (569–778). Dot under ϥ of ⲉϥⲁⲛϩ (1203, left of the descender). No strokes.

"leer" at the line end → vac.

Kephalaion number ⲓⲅ (13), centred, with a bar over it (946–981). Reconcile counts the line numeral.

Eight dots inside the brackets (578–762; 710 and 736 faint, area 4–5), one after them (797). Dots under ⲩ of ⲩⲕⲱⲛ (827), ⲥ and ⲉ of ⲛⲥⲉⲙⲧ[ⲁ]ⲛ (938, 951). Stroke over ⲙ (963–976).

Dots under ϩ (left of the descender, 815) and ⲟ (831) after the bracket, ⲛ of ⲡⲛⲟⲩⲥ (1028), ⲉ, ⲡ, ⲉ, ⲓ of ⲉⲡⲉⲓ (1228–1271; the dot of ⲓ at its foot). Diaereses over ⲓ of ⲁϩⲣⲏⲓ (925/930) and ⲟⲩⲁⲓⲛⲉ (1169/1175). Stroke over ⲛ of ⲛⲟⲩⲁⲓⲛⲉ (1104–1117).
The restoration [ⲇⲏ …] holds two restored letters and nineteen dots (639–1115) before the closing bracket (≈1126); four dots after it (1151–1230).
All ϣ on the page (ll. 5, 11, 28 twice, 29, 30; l. 1 restored) were checked at 6×; none is dotted.

The single dot after ⲡⲉ (1300, area 13) stands on the baseline like the illegible dots of the line (y 1631–1635) and is encoded as one illegible letter, not as a point sign (ledger §4). A faint grey speck below the dots at x ≈ 945 (not ink at the < 130 threshold, 8×) is not a sign. No strokes.
